# PERIANAL/ANORECTAL ABSCESS

Antibiotics should typically be reserved for patients with an anorectal abscess complicated by cellulitis, systemic signs of infection, underlying immunosuppression, or failure to improve with drainage alone. Cultures of abscess fluid are not routinely recommended. Consider in patients who will be treated with adjunctive antibiotic treatment for systemic signs of infection, recurrent infection or nonhealing wounds, or underlying immunosuppression.

## Primary therapy: abscess drainage

## _______________________________________________________________________________

## Adjunctive antimicrobial treatment for patients with above complications.

## Duration of treatment

5 days of antibiotics after incision and drainage is recommended. In the absence of source control, recommended duration is 7-14 days, based on severity of infection, underlying immunosuppression, and clinical response.

Therapy:
## Mild disease, outpatients, oral transition

Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h [R]

Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI]
< OR >
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h [DI]

## Inpatient

Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

Alternative:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

## Severe - critical illness

Preferred:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]

Alternative:
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
